pr.title: match lowering: consistently lower bindings deepest-first
pr.author: Nadrieril

analysis.originalLogic: Match lowering in `compiler/rustc_mir_build/src/build/matches/simplify.rs` accumulated bindings with special handling that distinguished refutable (tested) from irrefutable patterns. The patch title describes the old behavior: "Currently when lowering match expressions to MIR, we do a funny little dance with the order of bindings." The pre-fix code kept `existing_bindings`/`original_bindings` separate and, after simplification, combined original bindings with newly discovered nested bindings. This caused inconsistent ordering, including `x @ E::E { a, e: C { c } }` lowering the outer `@` binding before the nested field binding.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect transformation was to preserve source/left-to-right order for refutable bindings while reversing binding order only in some irrefutable cases. Patch 3's explanatory comment states: "// If however the bindings are refutable, i.e. under a test, then we keep the bindings" left-to-right. In the added regression test from Patch 1, this made both `x @ E::E{ a, e: C { c } }` and `mut x @ E::E{ a, e: C { mut c } }` emit `//~^ ERROR use of moved value`, because the outer `x` binding moved the enum before the nested `c`/field binding was copied out. Patch 4 is explicitly titled "Put new bindings first in refutable cases too", changing the combination to new bindings before original bindings; the final code removes those expected moved-value errors and uses deepest-first accumulation.
analysis.inputDomain: Match expressions and patterns that combine `@` bindings with nested destructuring bindings, especially refutable enum patterns and or-patterns. The relevant domain includes non-Copy structs/enums where moving the outer value before copying a `Copy` field changes borrow checking, e.g. `struct NonCopyStruct { copy_field: u32 }`, `enum E { E { a: i32, e: C }, NotE }`, `Option`, `Result`, tuples, arrays, and patterns like `x @ Ok(b) | x @ Err(b)`. Same-depth bindings such as `let (Some(a), Some(b)) = (x, y)` must remain in source order; deeper bindings must come before shallower `@` bindings. The refutable/irrefutable distinction is central to the input domain.
analysis.summary: A match-lowering bug-fix PR made binding order consistent by lowering deepest bindings first, while keeping bindings at the same depth in source order. Previously refutable patterns kept bindings left-to-right whereas irrefutable patterns used a different dance, causing `x @ Pat { field }` to bind the outer value before nested fields and produce erroneous borrow-check errors. The source-backed invariant is deepest-first, same-depth source order. MIR-opt tests for EarlyOtherwiseBranch were updated because the corrected lowering reorders StorageLive/assignment pairs in their input MIR.
analysis.trigger: Triggering conditions are match lowering of a candidate containing an `@` binding whose subpattern also contains bindings, especially when the pattern is refutable (under a test, e.g. an enum variant or an or-pattern) and the value/field is non-Copy. The historical inconsistency is described in the PR: "This leads to inconsistencies, as reported in https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/120210". The motivating example is `let y @ NonCopyStruct { copy_field: z } = x;`, where the field must be copied before `y` moves `x` because "the `y @` binding will move out of `x`, so we need to copy the field first."
preconditions: A match/let pattern contains an `@` binding together with nested bindings in its subpattern
The outer binding would move a non-Copy value, so nested field/copy bindings must be lowered first
Refutable patterns (tests, enum variants, or-patterns) are involved, because the old code treated them differently from irrefutable patterns
Same-depth bindings must not be reordered relative to source order
Or-pattern expansion must occur only after simplification reaches a fixed point; the PR moved the `Or` test out of the loop to do this consistently
pitfalls: Do not simply reverse all bindings: that breaks source order for same-depth bindings such as `let (Some(a), Some(b)) = (x, y)`
Do not preserve left-to-right order for refutable patterns: an outer `x @` binding can move the whole value before nested fields are copied, yielding a spurious use-of-moved-value error
The correct rule is deepest-first, and bindings at the same depth stay in source order
Do not conflate the refutable/irrefutable distinction with the later post-copy overwrite case; borrow restrictions and post-copy overwrites are separate conditions
The EarlyOtherwiseBranch MIR diffs only reflect reordered StorageLive/assignment sequences in the input MIR to that pass; they do not show EarlyOtherwiseBranch itself was fixed
Or-pattern handling timing matters: the patch moved the Or check out of the simplification loop and expands it only after fixed-point simplification
analysis.testStrategy: Add/extend run-pass UI tests under `tests/ui/pattern/bindings-after-at/`, especially `bind-by-copy.rs`, with both irrefutable struct destructuring and refutable enum patterns combining `@` and nested field bindings. The PR's new enum cases initially expected `//~^ ERROR use of moved value`; after the corrected transformation, Patch 4 restores `// run-pass` and removes those error annotations. Use the MIR-opt tests `tests/mir-opt/early_otherwise_branch*.diff` to check the expected binding order in lowered MIR: corrected output shows nested/deep bindings' `StorageLive`/assignment before the earlier one, e.g. `_9` then `_8` for a two-element case, and `_11`, `_12`, `_13` in reverse order for a three-element tuple. Also update borrowck UI expectations in `tests/ui/pattern/bindings-after-at/borrowck-*` when binding order changes diagnostics. No compiler was built, so these are source-inspection based test strategies, not executed results.
